blocks.title: What you'll learn
blocks.body:
**In this topic you'll learn:**

- The three stages of Alberta's Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) program and the rules at each stage
- What happens at the knowledge test and the road test
- How demerit points work, and when your licence is suspended
- What documents you must carry, and your responsibilities as a licence holder

Every new driver in Alberta goes through GDL, **regardless of age**.

blocks.title: Stage 1: Learner (Class 7)
blocks.body:
**To get a Class 7 learner's licence you must:**

- be **14** or older
- pass a vision screening and a **knowledge test**
- have **parental consent** if you are under 18
- have valid identification

**While you are a learner:**

- You must hold the learner's licence for at least **1 year**.
- A **fully licensed (non-GDL)** driver aged **18 or older** must sit **next to you**.
- You may **not drive from midnight to 5 a.m.**
- You may not carry **more passengers than seat belts**.
- You are suspended at **8 demerit points**.
- Your alcohol and drug level must be **zero**.

*Driver's Guide p. 10*

blocks.title: Stage 2: Probationary (Class 5-GDL)
blocks.body:
**To become a probationary driver you must:**

- have held your Class 7 for **1 year** (longer if you were suspended)
- be **16** or older
- pass the **Class 5 road test**

**While you are a probationary driver:**

- You stay probationary for at least **2 years**.
- You may not carry **more passengers than seat belts**.
- You are suspended at **8 demerit points**.
- Your alcohol and drug level must be **zero**.
- You **cannot supervise** a learner.
- You cannot upgrade to a commercial licence (Class 1, 2, 3, or 4).

The midnight-to-5 a.m. restriction applies to **learners only**, not probationary drivers.

*Driver's Guide p. 10*

blocks.title: Stage 3: Exiting GDL (full Class 5)
blocks.body:
**To leave the GDL program you must:**

- be at least **18**
- have been probationary for at least **2 years**
- have **no suspensions or traffic violations in the last 12 months**, including the zero alcohol and drug rule

An **approved driver training course** can shorten the probationary stage by **up to 6 months**.

**Once you have a full Class 5:** you can have more demerit points, the zero-tolerance condition is removed, you can supervise a learner, and you can upgrade to a commercial licence.

*Driver's Guide p. 11*

blocks.title: Parental consent
blocks.body:
Anyone **under 18** applying for a licence needs a parent or legal guardian to sign a consent form at a registry office.

- The parent or guardian can **withdraw consent in writing** at any time until the driver turns 18. The licence is then **suspended**.
- Consent is **not needed** if the minor can prove they are **married or self-supporting**.

The same rules apply to registering a vehicle.

*Driver's Guide pp. 16, 20*

blocks.title: The knowledge test and the road test
blocks.body:
**Knowledge test:** taken on a computer at a registry agent office, with multiple-choice questions based on the **Driver's Guide**: safe driving practices, driving laws, and road signs. It is available in 25 languages. There is a fee for each attempt, and you can take only **one test per day**.

**Class 5 road test:** about **45 minutes**, with no passengers or pets allowed. Your vehicle must be in good working order, with lights, horn, brakes, mirrors, seat belts, a clear windshield, good tires, valid plates and insurance, and enough fuel.

**Automatic fails**, no matter your score:

- speeding, or driving too fast for conditions
- not stopping completely at a stop sign, or before turning right on a red light
- failing to yield the right-of-way
- blocking traffic by driving too slowly or stopping unnecessarily
- climbing the curb while parking, or not parking legally within **3 attempts**
- not slowing down or checking properly at uncontrolled intersections

*Driver's Guide pp. 11–13, 15*

blocks.title: Documents and responsibilities
blocks.body:
- You must have your **driver's licence with you** whenever you drive.
- If a peace officer asks, you must show your **licence, registration, and insurance** (the "pink card").
- Every vehicle must be **registered** and **insured**. Driving an uninsured vehicle is illegal.
- You must report any **medical condition** that could affect your driving. That responsibility is yours, not your doctor's.
- If your licence is lost or stolen, replace it right away. If it was stolen, report it to police first.
- Keep your **address** up to date. Suspension notices are mailed to it.
- **New residents** from elsewhere in Canada can use their old licence for **90 days**, and must register their vehicle within **3 months**.

*Driver's Guide pp. 15–20*

blocks.title: Demerit points and suspensions
blocks.body:
Demerit points go on your record when you are **convicted** of an offence. That includes simply paying the ticket. Points are removed **2 years** after the conviction.

| | GDL drivers | Fully licensed drivers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warning letter | 4–7 points | 8–14 points |
| **Automatic suspension** | **8 points** | **15 points** |
| Points left after reinstatement | 3 | 7 |

**Suspension length:** 1st, **1 month**. 2nd within a year, **3 months**. 3rd within two years, **6 months**.

You can't appeal a demerit suspension, but you can ask for a review if you think points were assigned in error. An approved **defensive driving course** gives a **3-point credit**.

*Driver's Guide pp. 108–110*

blocks.title: Demerit points for common offences
blocks.body:
| Points | Offence |
| --- | --- |
| **7** | Leaving the scene of a collision |
| **6** | Careless driving · failing to stop for a school bus · racing · speeding 51+ km/h over |
| **5** | Failing to stop for a peace officer |
| **4** | Failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk · following too closely · speeding 31–50 km/h over |
| **3** | Running a stop sign or red light · failing to report a collision · improper passing · speeding 16–30 km/h over · distracted driving |
| **2** | Improper turn or U-turn · backing into an intersection or crosswalk · speeding up to 15 km/h over |
| **2** *(GDL only)* | Driving midnight–5 a.m. as a learner · more passengers than seat belts · supervisor not fully qualified |

*Driver's Guide pp. 91, 109–110*

blocks.title: Key numbers
blocks.body:
| What | Number |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum age, learner (Class 7) | **14** |
| Minimum age, probationary (Class 5-GDL) | **16** |
| Minimum age to exit GDL | **18** |
| Supervising driver | **18+**, fully licensed (non-GDL) |
| Minimum time as a learner | **1 year** |
| Minimum time as a probationary driver | **2 years** (up to **6 months** less with an approved course) |
| Violation-free period to exit GDL | last **12 months** |
| Learner curfew | **midnight to 5 a.m.** |
| Suspension: GDL / fully licensed | **8** / **15** points |
| Demerit points stay on record | **2 years** |
| New resident (from Canada) | **90 days** to switch licence |

blocks.title: Don't mix these up
blocks.body:
- **8 vs 15 points:** GDL drivers (learner *and* probationary) are suspended at 8. Fully licensed drivers are suspended at 15.
- **The curfew is for learners only.** Probationary drivers have no midnight-to-5 a.m. restriction.
- **Passengers vs seat belts** applies to **both** GDL stages.
- **The supervisor must be fully licensed (non-GDL) and 18+.** A probationary driver can't supervise, even if they are an adult.
- **Zero alcohol and drugs** applies to the whole GDL program, not just learners.
- **Reporting medical conditions is the driver's job,** not the doctor's or the employer's.
